pr_title: Allow Influxdb CA path in verify_ssl
pr_body:

## Breaking change
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Simple change to allow an optional CA path in the Influxdb configuration to verify SSL certificates. 
This applies to both V1 and V2 API.

```yaml
influxdb:
  ssl_ca_cert: /path/to/ca.crt
```

Additionally, `verify_ssl` is used for both V1 and V2 API.

## Type of change
<!--
  What type of change does your PR introduce to Home Assistant?
  NOTE: Please, check only 1! box!
  If your PR requires multiple boxes to be checked, you'll most likely need to

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml`:
<!--

```yaml
# Example configuration.yaml
influxdb:
  ssl: true
  ssl_cert_path: /path/to/ca.crt
  verify_ssl: true
```

@alexpilotti Sorry for the delay. Interesting, I wasn't aware of that. The InfluxDB client library says it only accepts a boolean but I see that it just passes it on as is to requests and requests accepts either a file or a boolean. Two comments:

1. What does the user see if they point to the wrong file? Does the log message make it clear how to fix it?
2. Is there any way to validate that it is a certificate file as part of config validation and not just that the file exists?

Also doc will need to be updated to mention that you can now use a path to a cert file in this option. And would you mind adding a test case to validate the new behavior?
I'm actually on the fence whether it just makes sense of adding a dedicated parameter for CA chain. influxdb choice of overloading `verify_ssl` to be boolean or a file path is not intuitive to me.
I'm on the boat of `just makes sense of adding a dedicated parameter for CA chain` myself

> @alexpilotti Sorry for the delay. Interesting, I wasn't aware of that. The InfluxDB client library says it only accepts a boolean but I see that it just passes it on as is to requests and requests accepts either a file or a boolean.

Yes, this is a common pattern in Python modules due how _requests_ uses _verify_ssl_. 

Here's an example of another integration component doing the same:
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tomato/#verify_ssl

Beside Python devs, this is not so user friendly for the rest of the population though. Since the config options for this module reflect the InfluxDBClient call parameters, I sticked to that, but we could add a _ca_path_ option instead if that's preferable.

> Two comments:
> 
> 1. What does the user see if they point to the wrong file? Does the log message make it clear how to fix it?

Like for other similar cases in the _InfluxDBClient_, the error bubbles up straight from the requests module:

`2021-01-27 00:04:28 ERROR (SyncWorker_1) [homeassistant.components.influxdb] Cannot connect to InfluxDB due to 'HTTPSConnectionPool(host='dummy', port=1234): Max retries exceeded with url: /write?db=home_assistant (Caused by SSLError(SSLError(136, '[X509: NO_CERTIFICATE_OR_CRL_FOUND] no certificate or crl found (_ssl.c:4265)')))'. Please check that the provided connection details (host, port, etc.) are correct and that your InfluxDB server is running and accessible. Retrying in 60 seconds.
`

If deemed useful, we could catch this particular SSLError and add a more explicit description of the error. 

> 2. Is there any way to validate that it is a certificate file as part of config validation and not just that the file exists?

The check is performed by the requests module's underlying SSL stack. There's usually no need to perform additional tests. 
There are countless examples in this codebase (e.g. the MQTT integration), just passing the provided CA file down the stack.

> 
> Also doc will need to be updated to mention that you can now use a path to a cert file in this option. And would you mind adding a test case to validate the new behavior?

Absolutely, on it :)

@Adminiuga @frenck as described in this comment https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/45270#issuecomment-767871650, I followed the way the options here just map the _InfluxDBClient_ client calls, and although there are other integrations in the codebase using this way of handling _verify_ssl_, I'm personally also in favor of a dedicated option (_ca_path_, or else).

@fabaff @mdegat01 please let me know what you guys think.

@fabaff @mdegat01 I added unit tests in the commit and also doc changes here:
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/16369

Can you please let me know if this is ok or if you prefer a separate option for the CA  certificate path as discussed above?

Thanks!

Looking at the V2 API, there's a `ssl_ca_cert` in https://github.com/influxdata/influxdb-client-python/blob/b6e3a0da70ad34022b61a88b772b7da2a8e6d141/influxdb_client/client/influxdb_client.py#L36, so IMO we could address both v1 and v2 use cases with a single config option. 

Note: there's also a `verify_ssl` arg in the V2 client, the HA `verify_ssl` boolean option should be applied to V2 as well.
Please add a dedicated config option for the cert file. 👍

Looks like tests are failing.

issue_context.title: Influxdb verify_ssl should allow a string for specifying a CA certificate
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

The influxdb configuration should allow a way to pass a CA certificate path.

Currently, it allows to specify _verify_ssl_, which requires a boolean. The underlying Python API allows either a boolean or a string containing the path to the CA certificate. Here's a simple example using Influxdb V1.xx:

```python
c = influxdb.InfluxDBClient(
    ssl=True, host="host", port=8086, username="user", password="password",
    verify_ssl='/path/to/ca.crt')
list(c.query("SHOW DATABASES", database="home_assistant").get_points())
[{'name': 'home_assistant'}]

```

Here's the schema requirement for _verify_ssl_:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/34a9b93d41396d794b42d08c5bad842f8fe6a372/homeassistant/components/influxdb/const.py#L147

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.1.4 
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Core 
- Integration causing this issue: influxdb
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/influxdb/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
influxdb:
  host: 192.168.1.190
  port: 20000
  database: DB_TO_STORE_EVENTS
  username: MY_USERNAME
  password: MY_PASSWORD
  ssl: true
  verify_ssl: true
```

## Traceback/Error logs

  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

